The unit is blowing warm air and the display flashes an alarm code. I have a pallet of chilled pharmaceuticals on board and the nearest depot is 3 hours away.
Customer complaints this week all mention the same thing: thawed prawns that smell off. Check the reefer on the route 7 trailers, which seems to run at plus 2 instead of minus 18.
An insulated shipper with plasma units reached the hospital with the temperature tag showing 11°C. They need to destroy the units and ask for urgent replacement.
Breakdown of the main compressor in the banana ripening room. The ripening schedule is lost and the fruit is already turning yellow too fast.
I opened the trailer at the destination and found water pooling on the floor. The defrost drain was blocked and the evaporator iced up, so cooling failed halfway.
A refrigerated truck's thermometer had been stuck at 4°C for the whole journey, but the actual cargo was at 13°C when we tested it with a handheld probe.
The warehouse generator did not take over during the blackout. The cold rooms for dairy were without power for 90 minutes and the temperature graph climbs steeply.
There is condensation dripping from the ceiling of our freezer corridor and the rear freezer room alarm shows minus 6°C. The door seal looks iced shut.
A cargo of fresh herbs shipped by air arrived with the gel packs fully melted. The airline left it on the apron for hours and the leaves are black and limp.
Our blood bank transport box lost its charge and displayed an error on the way. Samples are inside and the driver is 40 minutes from the lab.
The driver forgot to switch on the reefer after the last drop and drove two hours. Frozen dumplings are at minus 4°C and the bags have started to sweat.
The cold storage monitoring app has shown a red alert for zone 4 since midnight and nobody acknowledged it. The reading is 9°C where we need below 5°C for the dairy desserts.
A reefer trailer arrived at our site with its door unsealed and the box at 10°C. The driver says the unit was fine at pickup and blames the shipper for loading hot pallets.
We stored a batch of vaccines in a fridge that was damaged by a power spike. The data logger shows it climbed above 8°C for 4 hours overnight.
A defective refrigerant valve was found on the reefer after a long haul. Frozen chicken inside is at minus 7 and the customer wants to know if it is safe to receive.
Half the pallets of the supplier's ice cream shipment were frosted over inside the carton. This indicates thaw and refreeze cycles somewhere in the chain.
Chocolate bars shipped in summer arrived melted into the foil. The truck used was a normal box van, not a temperature controlled one, despite our instructions.
The air chute in the reefer was torn and cold air short-circuits back to the unit. The front pallets are at 2°C and the back ones are at 12°C.
The breakers tripped overnight at the pharma warehouse and freezer B stayed off for around five hours. We have biological samples inside and need a decision on whether to quarantine them.
Cold chain break at handover: the first carrier left the pallet in an open yard for the second carrier, and it stood there for two hours in the sun with fresh milk on it.
The meat packer says our chiller truck arrived at their dock with a core temperature of 8°C. They have asked for the reefer download and a corrective action report.
I think the thermostat setting got bumped. The load of flowers needs 3°C but the box shows 14°C. The petals have started to droop and I am an hour from the market.
The dry ice for our shipment of lab reagents ran out before delivery, and the package is now warm to the touch. The lab says the reagents must be kept frozen.
The fridge room at the cross-dock lost its cooling when a contractor cut the wrong cable. We moved a few pallets to another room but the rest are at 10°C.
One of our delivery vans has a faulty cold plate. The driver delivered frozen desserts to three customers before noticing it had stopped freezing. We need to recall those deliveries.
Customer reports that the cheese consignment smelled sour and the pallets were wet inside the wrap. The trailer log shows a long stop with the unit off at a border crossing.
An oyster shipment arrived with the display reading 15°C. Live shellfish must stay under 8, so the whole lot is going to be discarded.
The truck's reefer alarm shows high discharge pressure and the unit has stopped. I am parked on the shoulder and the load is frozen berries that cannot sit long.
A new employee turned off the freezer compressor to defrost the evaporator and forgot to turn it back on. Four hours later the product is at minus 5.
I dropped the trailer at the customer's yard and they had no power to plug the reefer in. The unit's diesel tank ran out and the inside is warming.
Our satellite temperature monitor shows spikes above 10°C every time the doors open at the three delivery stops, and the final stop receives goods near 9°C.
Insulin pens in the courier bag were left in a hot car for a day by mistake. The pharmacy says they cannot be sold and has requested a full replacement along with an incident record.
A seafood restaurant called to say that crab arrived barely cool and some were lifeless. Delivery was in an unrefrigerated van after our reefer broke at the hub.
The cold room sensor in Hall B reads minus 2°C but a product thermometer shows 7°C. We think the fixed sensor is miscalibrated, so the alarms never went off.
During a power outage the backup generator took 25 minutes to kick in. Our freezer went from minus 20 to minus 12 and the stock needs a quality review.
Fruit juice concentrate pallets were exposed to freezing weather in a winter storm and the cartons are bulging. The trailer heater failed and the temperature dropped to minus 8.
The pre-cooling of the trailer was skipped by the loading crew. I noticed the display read 18°C when we sealed the doors, and the frozen pizzas are already softening.
A reefer trailer on its way to the airport has a broken fan belt. The box is warming slowly and the pharmaceutical consignment has to make a flight in four hours.
Quality control found strawberries with mould and soft spots after the trailer log showed a six-hour period at 15°C. The retailer has rejected 20 pallets.
One of the display fridges in our depot shop failed overnight and we lost a full pallet of fresh pasta. The log shows it was at room temperature by morning.
A truck with frozen vegetables was stuck behind a breakdown and the driver switched off the reefer to conserve fuel. By the time he restarted, the box was at minus 2.
The sensor probe wire in the trailer was chewed by something and is giving false low readings. The product is actually warm. We need all trailers on this route checked.
Seafood paste shipments from our supplier have been arriving above the contract limit for three weeks in a row, the last one at 8°C. Stop shipping until the issue is found.
A leaking reefer hose sprayed coolant onto the floor and the unit lost pressure. The load of chilled juice is at 9°C and the driver has called for roadside help.
Operators noted that the blast chiller did not reach its target in the required time. A cooked rice batch is at 28°C after two hours when it should be below 10.
Customer complained of icy crystals and a freezer-burn smell on ice cream cartons. They believe the load was left at the dock too long before being put into cold storage.
The reefer door flapped open on a bumpy road because the latch bar was bent. We lost cold air for maybe an hour. The yoghurt cartons at the rear are at 11°C.
Our two-day shipment of cultured cells for a research lab was held up in customs without refrigeration and is now showing 22°C on the tag. They need to be told immediately.
I noticed ice building up on the reefer's evaporator and almost no airflow. The display says 6°C setpoint but the real temperature of the box is around 12°C.
A delivery of salad kits arrived at 13°C inside the trailer. The driver says the reefer was left on ventilation mode instead of cooling mode by the previous driver.
Warehouse worker here: the freezer door's heater strip failed, the door is frozen half open, and the air near the entrance is minus 4 instead of minus 22.
The tag recorder on our frozen seafood container expired and shows no data, so we cannot prove the cold chain. The buyer is refusing payment until a record is provided.
A landslide has cut off the road to the mountain hospital and I am on the far side with oxygen concentrators. I need an alternate route or other transport option as soon as possible.
The truck taking livestock vaccines to the farm cooperative is stuck behind an overturned lorry and the vaccines must be administered tomorrow morning. No alternate route known.
Our driver got sick and cannot continue. Nine pallets of fresh bread for a hotel chain are sitting in the cab and there is no relief driver within 150 km.
Port congestion has delayed our container of car seats by four days and the car plant's line stops tomorrow noon. They are charging 20,000 dollars an hour in penalties.
The tailgate lift broke at the hospital loading bay and I cannot unload the dialysis machines. The nurse says they are needed on the ward within two hours.
Heavy snow closed the pass and 12 trucks are waiting. The cargo includes fresh milk for a school meal program that expires in two days.
Our carrier missed the sailing and the next vessel leaves in 10 days. The exhibition stand materials are needed in Dubai by Monday.
The truck engine seized outside the city limits. The chilled sushi for tonight's restaurant opening has 3 hours of shelf life left and nobody else can reach it in time.
Customs has seized the paperwork and is holding the truck of spare parts for a stopped production line. The client says every hour of delay costs them tens of thousands.
We have the largest wedding of the year tomorrow and the flower truck is stuck on the highway in a flooded section. Delivery needs to be done by 6 PM today.
The ambulance equipment shipment was left behind at the air hub because the manifest was wrong. The county health office needs it by morning for a mass vaccination event.
My trailer's brake lines failed and the truck has been towed. The load is human blood samples for a transplant centre and they have a 5-hour window.
The truck is delayed by 6 hours because of a bridge closure and the cargo is live lobsters that need to reach the restaurant by tonight or they will die.
Our trailer was held at the border due to a driver permit problem. The chemicals inside are needed at a water treatment plant tomorrow or the city will run out of purifying agents.
The cross-dock sorter jammed and 40 trailers of Black Friday stock are late. The retailer says unless it arrives by 6 AM they will cancel the orders and charge us a penalty.
A tire explosion damaged the suspension and the truck cannot move. The delivery is a set of aircraft parts for a grounded plane waiting at the airport.
We missed the last ferry and the next one is tomorrow afternoon. The cargo of bakery items for an event tonight cannot wait, so we need another way across right now.
Driver hours are exhausted and the truck is at a layby 30 km from the destination. The load is donor tissue cultures for a clinic, due in the next hour. Please send a relief driver.
A protest has blocked the entry to the factory and trucks with production inputs cannot get in. The plant says it will stop its line within the next two hours.
The truck with copper cathodes for the smelter is two days late and the smelter has run out of feed material. They have started to lose money every hour.
A heat wave buckled the pavement on the highway and traffic has been diverted by 200 km. My cargo is fresh strawberries for a festival that opens at 9 AM tomorrow.
A flight was cancelled so our urgent courier parcel with signed legal contracts will miss the filing deadline today. We need another way to reach the court office by 4 PM.
Our tanker is stuck in a 6-hour queue at the fuel depot, and the hospital generators are down to a few hours of diesel. They will lose backup power if we do not arrive.
A landslip on the line means the cargo train carrying sugar for a beverage plant will not arrive for a week. The plant has one day of stock and production will stop tomorrow.
I had to stop for a repair on the road, and the vaccines will miss the cold chain window if I do not get a replacement truck in two hours.
The truck delivering election material to polling stations is held up by a flooded road. The vote is tomorrow and the material must be in place by evening.
The airline overbooked the freight and our cargo of insulin cartridges was offloaded. The pharmacy distributor says stock-outs are happening and patients are calling.
A pileup shut the expressway and I am stuck for hours with a truckload of cut roses for Valentine's Day at a supermarket chain whose delivery slot closes at noon.
The third-party courier has lost track of a package containing a spare part for a hospital MRI machine. The machine is down and patients are being redirected elsewhere.
The truck delivering the replacement pump to the flooded mine broke its axle. Water is rising in the lower shaft and the crew needs the pump today.
Traffic around the stadium after the match added about 40 minutes to my trip. The customer's receiving hours run until 6 PM so there is plenty of time.
The depot loaded my truck late because the forklift was being serviced. I will be a few hours behind but the goods are regular warehouse replenishment.
Strong crosswinds slowed everyone down on the bridge. I should arrive about an hour late at the retail park, and the store manager is aware.
Customer email asking why their tracking page has said in transit for three days. The carrier says there was a minor hub backlog and expects delivery on Friday.
Lane closures from road resurfacing near the exit are causing a 20-minute queue. Nothing urgent on board, just office stationery for a regular order.
Our weekly pallet shipment from the regional DC will arrive Wednesday instead of Tuesday because of a carrier driver shortage. The store has enough on shelves until then.
Slight delay at the port gate this morning as the system was down for 45 minutes. The container has no hard deadline and we can pick it up tomorrow.
My GPS took me through a school zone and I lost about 30 minutes on narrow streets. I will make the afternoon window for the paint delivery as planned.
The courier says the parcel will be a day late because the van needed a tire change. It contains a replacement phone cover so there is no rush.
Early evening rain flooded one lane near the exit and cars are crawling. I am about an hour behind schedule but the customer closes at 8.
The shipment of garden furniture slipped from Monday to Thursday since the previous vessel was full. The customer has been told and does not mind.
There was a queue at the weighbridge because of an audit and we lost two hours. The cargo is cement bags and the site manager says tomorrow morning is fine as well.
A lorry in front of me shed a load of straw and traffic stopped for half an hour. I will still reach the depot before it shuts.
The booking for our dock slot was cancelled by the warehouse because of a staff shortage and moved to the next day. Our stock is not urgent so the change is acceptable.
I have a five-hour slip on my planned arrival due to a breakdown of the previous driver's truck. The customer just called back and said it is fine to deliver next morning.
Three trucks ahead of me had paperwork problems at the gate, so I will unload late this afternoon instead of at noon. Pallets of books, nothing perishable.
Foggy at dawn on the ring road. The convoy is moving at 30 km per hour so I will be about two hours late to the distribution centre. They said no problem.
The truck made an extra stop to return a damaged pallet to origin and that added an hour. The remainder will still be delivered on the same day.
The annual holiday pushed the sorting centre's volume to a peak, so deliveries in our region are running a day late. Customers have been notified by SMS.
The customer's gate guard was not at his post and I waited an hour with the engine on. The delivery of floor tiles is going ahead after that, and the foreman is not worried.
A parade closed the main street and I had to take the long way around. I expect to arrive after lunch, which is still within the retailer's receiving window.
The order confirmation says two days but tracking now says four. It is a set of kitchen chairs and I am not in a hurry, just curious about the reason.
The truck was assigned a different route because of a new road permit requirement and the trip will take 90 minutes longer. The receiving party was informed this morning.
Light snow overnight meant trucks left the yard late. About 20 deliveries are running 1 to 2 hours behind but all of them are standard retail orders.
Driver changeover at the depot was late because the relief driver overslept. I took over the truck 70 minutes later than planned and will still deliver today.
There was a short delay with our container at inspection because the customs officer needed one more signature. It was cleared in the afternoon and the importer was fine with it.
Delivery to the warehouse was pushed because their dock was full of trucks, and they asked us to come back tomorrow. Our load is dry goods and the rescheduled slot works for everyone.
A slow-moving farm vehicle on a single-lane road made me late by about 25 minutes. The consignee is an office and told me to just come when I can.
A heavy downpour made the underpass impassable for an hour, but it has reopened. I will be late for the 3 PM slot but the receiver has moved me to 4.
My truck had to wait at the railway crossing for a freight train that was stopped for more than 30 minutes. It is a clothes order for a boutique, and delivery is still on time for tomorrow.
We ordered 40 reams of 80 gsm paper and a pallet arrived with 70 gsm. The pallet tag and invoice both say 80 gsm so I think the picker grabbed the neighbouring stock.
The customer ordered the 2-liter version of the water jug but the cartons contain the 1-liter. Both products share the same shelf and the same packaging colour.
The pallet we received for store 14 has the label for store 41. The content is right for the other store, so the transposed digits happened during labelling.
Packed order 90455 shows two blenders, but the box contains one blender and one toaster. The picker mis-scanned an adjacent SKU.
I opened the carton of men's socks and found women's socks in a similar colour. Same product code except for the last letter. Please send the correct pairs.
We received 5 boxes of gloves in size small when we asked for large. Our staff have already opened two boxes and need replacements by Friday.
Instead of the 12 pack of AA batteries, the order contained 12 single AAA packs. The quantity matches but the type is wrong.
One line of our order is missing altogether: 10 desk lamps. The packing slip lists them as shipped, yet there are only 9 items in the box.
A picker took stock from the quarantine area and sent it out. The units have a hold sticker on them and were not cleared by quality.
We got another customer's order in our delivery. Their name is on the packing slip and they ordered a different kind of cat litter.
The supplier sent the right quantity of bolts but in zinc finish instead of stainless steel. Our job requires stainless and the zinc ones will rust outdoors.
I need to flag a pick error: we ordered 6 left-hand door handle sets and got 6 right-hand ones. The case labels are correct, so the wrong goods are inside the right cases.
We were shipped 100 units of the old model number even though the system shows it as replaced. Whoever picked the order chose from an old shelf location.
Today's delivery has twice the quantity we wanted on four lines. It looks like a unit of measure confusion, cases versus each.
Two sizes of the same shirt style were stacked in one bin and the picker mixed them in the order. The customer got sizes M and L in the same carton labelled M.
We were sent 24 bottles of hot sauce in mild rather than extra hot. The label on the case says extra hot but the bottles inside are mild.
Mispick in aisle 22: the bin labelled 8 mm drill bits actually contained 6 mm, which has caused a few wrong orders this week.
A customer got a shipping box containing someone else's headphones. Their own order of a webcam is still sitting on our packing bench.
On receiving, I counted 18 cartons but the paperwork and our PO say 24. Six cartons were not picked even though the picking sheet is ticked.
The goods came with a lot number that expires next month. For this item we ordered a minimum remaining shelf life of 6 months. The picker chose the oldest lot.
Orders for two branches of the same pharmacy chain were swapped. Branch A has the vitamins for B and vice versa. The pallet labels were mixed at the packing area.
The client ordered black ink cartridges and received yellow. Item numbers are one apart, and the picker likely read the wrong digit on the pick list.
The wrong fabric colour was cut and packed for a bulk order. They wanted navy and we sent charcoal rolls totalling 300 meters.
The customer complains that the toy set arrived without the batteries that were included in the product description. The picker forgot to add the accessory pack to the bundle.
Our driver delivered 4 pallets but the order was for 5. The WMS shows 5 loaded, which means a pallet was ticked but not loaded, or loaded onto the wrong truck.
The pick team sent a box of A4 lined notebooks instead of the squared ones that were ordered. Both are in the same stack and have similar covers.
When I unpacked the order, the cookware lids were for a 24 cm pan but the pans are 28 cm. The pairs were split during picking.
The wrong region variant of a game console was dispatched. The customer needs the EU version and got the US one, with the wrong plug.
Our order included 30 extra units of an item that we did not request, and one of the ones we asked for is missing. Possibly an off-by-one in the SKU.
The labels on shelf A-07 were switched after a re-slotting exercise, and since then we have had four mispicks involving shower heads and taps.
A customer returned an unopened box of hair dryers, but the box held hair straighteners. The mix-up occurred at dispatch because the two share a single product page.
Our order for 10 laptop sleeves of 13 inch arrived as 10 sleeves of 15 inch. They will not fit, and the customer wants a swap by Monday.
We were shipped sugar-free biscuits when the order was for regular biscuits. The cartons look nearly the same and the picker missed the small text.
The picker used the wrong batch for the pharmaceutical order. The strength was 10 mg and the order said 5 mg, so the stock was held at receiving and reported.
A retailer received a pallet intended for another retailer, consisting of seasonal items they never ordered. They have photographed the labels.
The delivery note says 3 monitors with HDMI cables, but the box has no cables. The cable bundle line was skipped in picking.
The customer wanted three-hole paper and got two-hole paper. The stock code differs by a single suffix and the picker did not read it fully.
The invoice says 20 spare filters for model X200, and the filters inside are for the X300. They do not fit, and the mismatch was only discovered at installation.
A customer was sent the wrong colour paint on a trade order. They asked for white and got cream. The tins have a small colour dot which the picker overlooked.
Eight items in the shipment were not on our order, and the sales rep says the customer ordered under a similar account name. The picker used the wrong account.
The pallet of juice we received has pineapple instead of orange. The outer wrap reads orange and the packing slip says orange too, so the pallet was probably built from the wrong location.
This morning's outbound audit found 14 orders with an incorrect pack count. It looks like a scale issue at the packing station, so picks are being checked again.
We found a pallet of our goods in the aisle designated for another customer. If the picker had taken it, there would have been another wrong shipment.
Our order of 200 pens included 200 refill packs and no pens. They are the same price and sit next to each other.
Instead of left-handed baseball gloves, we got right-handed. The packaging only gives the size in large print, which is probably what the picker looked at.
The customer ordered a 55-inch TV and a 43-inch one was packed. The model number on the carton looks right to a casual glance, but the screen size differs.
A wrong delivery address label was applied to a pallet in the dispatch bay and it went to the neighbouring town. The customer has been calling and wants the right goods.
Warehouse replenishment sent the wrong flavour of protein powder to the gym chain. They requested vanilla and received chocolate for eight tubs.
We found out that two pickers had been scanning the wrong barcode, the one on the outer shrink, which is the same for two different products. This explains the recent errors.
The sample pack we sent to a prospect had the wrong brochure inside, an old price list from last year. Quite embarrassing and needs to be replaced.
An order of gift boxes went out with the Christmas design instead of the Diwali design. The customer is a retailer who needs them for next month.
The customer wanted 12 packs of A5 sticky notes but got 12 packs of A7. The codes for the sizes differ by only a digit and the picker went with the closest bin.
Our system showed picks completed, yet the delivery came 15 pieces short. The picker scanned the case once but the case contains only 5 pieces instead of 20.
A cat food order contained dog food of the same brand. The customer has opened one carton and cannot return it, so would like a replacement.
The pick list had the wrong unit of measure and the warehouse sent 6 single bottles instead of 6 cases of detergent. The customer is understandably annoyed.
We shipped a size 10 shoe to a customer who ordered size 8. Customer service confirmed the size on the order, so the error happened at the picking stage.
The wrong colour cables were sent for a data centre order, blue instead of the specified grey. Colour coding matters for them and they need all 60 swapped.
The order was packed correctly, but the pick team put the paperwork for a different customer inside the carton. The invoice amounts do not match what is in the box.
We have a spare part for the wrong machine generation in the order. The part number on the label ends with B but the part is for version C.
We delivered the right products in the wrong quantity per carton, 6 per carton rather than 12. The customer wanted to re-stock vending machines and has to do some repacking.
The shrink wrap on the delivered pallet had been ripped off on one side and 6 cartons at the corner were crushed. Contents seem alright but the cartons look like they were hit by a forklift.
Rainwater got into the load on the way and the bottom layer of sacks of rice are soaked. The pallet is heavy and the bags are splitting when lifted.
Two cartons of wine arrived with wet bottoms and a strong smell of alcohol. At least four bottles broke and the cardboard has gone soft.
Cardboard boxes of bathroom tiles had their corners crumpled and a number of tiles chipped at the edges. The pallet was not strapped and the load shifted.
During offloading the forklift driver pushed a fork through the side of a carton of olive oil tins. Two tins are dented and one has leaked a little onto the pallet.
An entire row of cartons is caved in on the pallet because another pallet was stacked on top of it. The goods inside are electrical sockets, which seem fine, but the packaging is flattened.
The drum of cooking oil has a hairline crack along the seam and there is a small puddle in the trailer. Not a hazardous product, but it needs cleaning and the drum is unusable.
The cartons of crockery arrived with the sides bulging and rattling, and the dividers had collapsed. We opened one and about a third of the plates had broken edges.
All the bags of cement on the bottom layer are hard and lumpy because they got wet. The pallet's plastic cover was never applied.
Several cartons were bent in the middle, as if the pallet was dropped from a height. Mirrors inside have chipped corners and were packed with only thin foam.
Outer cartons of our books have mould spots on them as the pallet was stored in a damp area. The books inside are mostly fine but the covers are stuck to the wrapper.
The garment boxes were chewed through at the corners by rodents at the carrier's warehouse. There are droppings and holes in 5 boxes and the clothes need to be inspected.
The wooden crate carrying a glass table top arrived with a split side. The glass had a visible crack across it and there was no corner protection.
One side of the pallet was dragged across the floor and the bottoms of the cartons are torn and scuffed. The goods inside, paper cups, are still sealed.
A leaking bottle of soy sauce had soaked the cartons beneath it and left a sticky mess on four of the boxes. The labels are unreadable.
Many of the boxes of cereal were crushed flat on the top layer because the pallet height was above the trailer's recommended limit.
Crates of eggs on the pallet were crushed at the base and about 8 trays were broken, leaving a mess on the pallet and the floor of the trailer.
Cartons of dishwasher tablets came with split seams and the powder has spilled into the plastic wrap. The rest of the pallet has a chemical smell.
A box of ceramic sinks was punctured by the fork of a pallet truck, and one sink has a visible chip on the rim. The delivery driver said it happened on the way in.
The plastic container lids arrived cracked and warped because the pallet sat in the sun at a loading dock all afternoon.
During transit the tape came off a carton of glassware and the flaps opened. Two glasses fell out and shattered, and several more are chipped.
Several 20 kg sacks of fertilizer were torn open and product has leaked onto the other sacks. The trailer floor is covered with granules.
Multiple cartons of tinned tomatoes have dents in the side and the labels are scuffed. The cans are not leaking but the supermarket will not accept dented cases.
The customer says the corner protectors on the television boxes were missing and the packaging is dented on three of the boxes. Screens seem alright but they do not want to take a chance.
We received a pallet of canvas paintings in cartons with crushed edges. One canvas has a dent in the frame and another has a tear across the surface.
Four 25-litre containers of liquid soap were cracked on the way, leaving the pallet slimy. The shrink film trapped the liquid, so everything under it is wet.
The outer cases of baby formula tins look battered and crumpled and one case is soaked on one side. The inner tins are fine but the retailer will only accept clean cases.
The strapping on a pallet of steel pipes broke and several pipes slid out and dented the pallet next to it. A few pallet boards are splintered too.
A heavy carton fell off the top of a stack in the warehouse and landed on a box of lampshades. They are crushed beyond use.
The foam inserts in the box for the printer were missing, and the printer has a cracked panel on the side. The box has a visible puncture mark.
The rear of the trailer had a puddle from a roof leak. Pallets were standing in water for a long time and the bottom cartons of paper towels have turned to mush.
The pallet of jars of pickles had two broken jars and the brine ran down through the cartons, so all cartons under them are soggy and about to collapse.
A delivery of mattresses in plastic arrived with oil stains and tears in the wrap. The mattresses are not damaged but the customer cannot accept soiled packaging.
A few of the boxes of light bulbs sound like they are full of broken glass when shaken. The cartons were put under a heavier pallet of tiles.
The cardboard tubes holding posters were bent and flattened at one end. The rolled posters inside have creases and some are torn.
The container arrived with condensation dripping from the roof and a layer of rust spots on the steel components in cartons. The cartons are damp and the labels are peeling.
The pallet jack operator dropped a box containing a glass display case. Fragments are everywhere and the box is open, while the other boxes nearby have glass shards on them.
A shipment of musical instruments had a dented guitar case and a scratched violin box. The packaging didn't have enough padding and the cartons were stacked three high.
One side of the trailer had an empty space and the load of mixed cartons shifted. Roughly 10 of them are open, with products scattered on the trailer floor.
We found the bottom three cartons of laundry liquid cracked and leaking in our storeroom. There is a lot of mess and the floor is slippery, so the stack needs to be moved carefully.
The cardboard sleeves for the picture frames got wet and bent. The frames themselves are fine, but the packaging cannot go on the shelf.
A truck door was damaged and the cartons nearest to it have scrape marks and gashes. The customer wants a photo-based claim for packaging damage.
Heavy bags of rice were stacked on top of cartons of biscuits and the biscuit cartons are crushed. Crumbs are visible through the torn edges.
We found tears in the outer wrap of 8 pallets coming from the same supplier this week, and a number of cartons are scuffed. We suspect poor wrapping at the source.
Cartons of cooking spray cans were dropped and some cans are visibly dented and a couple have leaked propellant. The pallet should be kept apart.
The glass bottles of juice were not separated by dividers and ten of them broke in transit. The rest of the box is sticky and the cartons are collapsing.
The outer boxes for the microwaves are dented at the corners and one has a hole where a strap bit into it. The customer wants to check each unit before accepting.
A pallet of printed brochures arrived with water stains running through the whole stack. The top ones are fine but the lower half is stuck together and curled up.
A box of wedding invitations got creased in the middle when something heavy was put on it. The envelopes are bent and a few are torn, and they are due for dispatch.
Dozens of fruit crates were cracked because the wooden slats were too thin for the load. The fruit has bruised and the outer layer is squashed.
Crates of beer bottles were stacked badly and the bottom crate buckled. Two dozen bottles broke and the plastic crates are cracked.
The corrugated boxes of toys were crushed and are folded like an accordion. The packaging is flattened but the toys inside seem fine. The retailer says it cannot be sold in this state.
The strap on the pallet was too tight and cut into the boxes, leaving deep creases and slits in the top row.
Barrels of paint arrived with dented lids and a few drips down the sides. The label on one barrel is smeared and unreadable. It is not leaking much but the barrel is messy.
The load of mirrors had corner damage. Several mirrors have chipped edges because the crate had no padding and was packed too loosely.
We got a complaint about bags of peas torn at the seam. The bags were mishandled by the carton packers and the peas are scattered inside the box.
The metal cabinets arrived with dents on the doors from rubbing against each other. The protective film is torn and the paint is scratched on three units.
During unloading a pallet toppled in the yard and about 20 cartons of snack packs split open. The snack packs are crushed and scattered and will need to be written off.
Plastic wrap around the pallet was never fitted and the cartons shifted into each other, leaving bent corners and torn flaps on several of them.
Rodents chewed through the sacks of lentils stored at the warehouse. Several sacks have holes and grains on the floor, and the pallet is contaminated and needs to be removed.
